title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
task: Learning unified tactile representation across heterogeneous sensors for dexterous manipulation
key_results: LingBot-Touch enables plug-and-play integration across piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors; consistently improves manipulation performance on real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms
comments: Strong practical contribution addressing sensor diversity, though evaluation primarily focuses on task success rather than transfer learning metrics across sensor types.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cross-sensor tactile representations can transfer between diverse sensor hardware
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; unified tokens work across multiple sensors and hardware platforms

title: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
task: Unified infrastructure and evaluation for generative world models across modalities
key_results: WorldFoundry catalog: 270 models, 74 benchmarks, 62 metrics; enables reproducible comparison of persistent, controllable dynamics across video, 3D/4D, embodied, and interactive systems
comments: Excellent infrastructure contribution but lacks concrete performance comparisons; value lies in standardization and reproducibility rather than novel methods.

title: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
task: Post-training visual agents to align observations and handle tool-returned data in RL/distillation
key_results: Reframe outperforms Mix-RL and vanilla MOPD across 14 image/video benchmarks; GD-GRPO increases observation dependence and tool gain vs outcome-based GRPO
comments: Novel observation-alignment perspective in distillation, though the two-stage approach adds complexity; gains appear incremental on individual benchmarks.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stochastic removal of visual input encourages grounded observation use
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; GD-GRPO increases tool-observation dependence

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mid-rollout observation repair improves distillation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; OG-MOPD shows gains when combined with GD-GRPO

title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
task: Metacognitive architecture for scientific discovery and ideation
key_results: Sage-Taiyi ranks first on Taiyi-Bench (54.0 vs 47.9 baseline); validated chemistry yields: cobalt-catalyzed carbonylation 0% → 84%, photocatalytic allylic amination 13% → 69%
comments: Impressive empirical validation with real experimental results; metacognition-inspired design is novel but the paper's depth on mechanism remains unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Explicit monitoring and control of evidence/assumptions improves scientific ideation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; strong performance on historical rediscovery and open-ended tasks

hypotheses.hypothesis: AI-guided optimization can improve real chemical synthesis yields
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; dramatic yield improvements in two chemistry reactions

title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
task: Standardized artifact design and agent workflows for reproducible ML experiments
key_results: ReproBridge-Bench: 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments; refined artifacts raise reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6%, reduce API cost by 19.7%, narrow model spread from 21.6 to 3.9 percentage points
comments: Pragmatic contribution showing execution knowledge matters for reproducibility; standardized artifacts are impactful but the approach is straightforward engineering.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Preserving execution knowledge improves agent reproduction success
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; refined artifacts raise success from 76.4% to 92.6% across models

title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
task: Efficient inference engine for decision models in LLM agent systems
key_results: Flide: 9.5× faster than vLLM/SGLang on decision model queries; exact arithmetic with ForkAttention; stays closest to float32 reference in total variation distance
comments: Strong systems contribution with clear speedup; the decoupling of logical and physical execution is elegant, though specialized to decision-tree workloads.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Decoupling logical tree structure from physical execution enables exact, efficient inference
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ForkAttention maintains exactness with 9.5× speedup

title: SIRIS: Can LLMs Tell When Simulation Errors Matter in AI-Driven Systems Research
task: Evaluating LLM ability to judge when simulator errors invalidate systems design recommendations
key_results: Frontier LLMs cannot reliably distinguish valid from invalid simulator-based recommendations; self-correction helps but introduces new errors; even identifying limitations does not ensure correct choice
comments: Important diagnostic showing systems reasoning gaps in LLMs; limited in scope (LLM serving problems) but highlights a critical real-world failure mode.

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLMs can distinguish valid from invalid simulator recommendations
hypotheses.result: Partially rejected; models struggle on perturbed simulators

title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
task: Understanding training-inference mismatch tolerance in on-policy distillation
key_results: OPD tolerates substantial quantization mismatch without quality loss up to empirical budget; FP8 recipes preserve quality with 1.93× more KV-cache tokens than BF16; synchronous BF16 training reaches same quality 1.62× slower
comments: Thorough empirical investigation with practical implications; the admitted-check screening mechanism is useful for practitioners, though findings are somewhat incremental.

hypotheses.hypothesis: OPD tolerates substantial quantization without quality loss
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; empirical mismatch budget characterized

hypotheses.hypothesis: Weight noise shifts prefixes in ways per-token corrections cannot fix
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; analysis reveals limitation of simple corrections

title: TRIO: Task Refinement with Individual Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
task: Multi-agent task refinement with iterative optimization for retrieval-augmented generation
key_results: TRIO outperforms state-of-the-art across multiple benchmark datasets; effective at improving answer quality through query extension, unanimity voting, and curriculum-learned answer generation
comments: Solid multi-agent refinement approach with clear reward alignment; evaluation spans multiple benchmarks but lacks explicit quantitative comparisons to baselines.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Aligning individual agent objectives improves RAG performance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; TRIO outperforms baselines across benchmarks

title: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
task: Adapting RL objectives for few-step diffusion models
key_results: Few-step versions of FlowGRPO, AWM, DiffusionNFT, DiffusionOPSD, ReFL in single modular codebase; reward-gradient methods most effective when reward is differentiable; extra inference steps show no systematic aggregate benefit
comments: Principled adaptation framework with thorough ablations; however, practical speedup gains over many-step models remain unclear from abstract.

hypotheses.hypothesis: RL objectives adapt to few-step diffusion via transformation and decomposition
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; modular codebase achieves this for multiple objectives

hypotheses.hypothesis: Extra inference steps provide systematic benefit
hypotheses.result: Rejected; no consistent improvement in aggregate reward

title: AutoVend: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Vending Operations
task: Evaluating LLM agents on long-horizon autonomous vending machine operations
key_results: AutoVend benchmark: 20 machines, 5 site types, 180 days; 4 of 5 LLM agents underperform rule-based baseline; gains in individual metrics do not translate to economic growth; returns per inference dollar rank differently from absolute returns
comments: Important real-world alignment study; highlights failures in grounding, inventory management, and feedback utilization, though simulation fidelity assumptions warrant scrutiny.

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLM agents can optimize O2O commerce operations over 180 days
hypotheses.result: Largely rejected; most underperform baseline on economic returns

title: JoVox: Joint Hierarchical Flow Matching for Lightweight Voxel Generation
task: Lightweight high-fidelity voxel generation via joint hierarchical flow matching
key_results: JoVox: 8× higher training throughput, 1/15 FLOPs vs TRELLIS.2, trains on 4 vs 32 GPUs; 11% lower Chamfer distance; outperforms on unconditional and image-conditioned generation
comments: Strong efficiency improvements with the joint hierarchy insight; the two-level prediction and unmasking strategy are sensible optimizations, though gains are primarily efficiency rather than quality.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Finer cells should inform coarse cell generation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; joint hierarchy outperforms level-by-level generation

title: InfraRSI: Harnessing Recursive Self-Improvement for Training Infrastructure
task: Recursive self-improvement for distributed LLM training infrastructure optimization
key_results: InfraRSI: up to 2.75× speedup, lifts MFU from 17.4% to 30.0% across dense and MoE workloads; outperforms existing tuners while transferring experience across GPUs
comments: Sophisticated agentic approach with verification mechanisms and experience distillation; the two-level RSI loop is innovative, though evaluation focuses on speedup without discussing potential hidden costs.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Recursive self-improvement can optimize tightly coupled training infrastructure
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; achieves substantial speedup and efficiency gains

title: How Many Exposures Does a World Model Need? Learning Unseen Game Mechanics at Test Time
task: Learning unseen game mechanics at test time with world models
key_results: WARC learns 4 in 5 mechanics with 80% accuracy on cell changes; half reach 80% within ~80 exposures; WARC-Agent triples graph-explorer efficiency from 0.15 to 0.46; Kaggle leaderboard score 0.20
comments: Interesting test-time learning evaluation on ARC-AGI; the MechEval benchmark is well-motivated, though limited to visual interactive games and leaderboard scores remain modest.

hypotheses.hypothesis: World models can learn unseen mechanics from limited test-time exposure
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; achieves 80% accuracy within single gameplay session

title: SkinMind: Equipping Agentic RAG with Human-Inspired Graph Probing for Reliable Dermatology AI
task: Multimodal agentic RAG for evidence-grounded dermatology reasoning
key_results: SkinMind improves average score by 8.70–8.89 points on 6 VQA benchmarks vs direct answering; outperforms competing RAG methods; KG: 1.0M nodes, 2.0M edges from 62M-token corpus and 423K images
comments: Well-designed multimodal system with human-inspired graph probing; domain expertise integration is strong, though evaluation on VQA may not fully capture clinical decision-making complexity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Graph probing enables more effective multimodal evidence retrieval than flat RAG
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; consistent improvements on VQA benchmarks

title: Training Vision Transformers to Focus: Emergence of Spatial Attention Head Specialization
task: Improving spatial attention head specialization in Vision Transformers via focusing loss
key_results: Focusing loss increases spatial selectivity and diversity of attention heads; improves performance on dense prediction tasks (zero-shot segmentation) without annotations; substantially increases interpretability
comments: Clean self-supervised method without ground-truth annotations; focusing loss concept is straightforward, though quantitative improvements and generalization to non-dense tasks remain unclear.

model_io.model: Vision Transformer with visual focusing loss

hypotheses.hypothesis: Visual focusing loss establishes correspondence between attention and image regions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; leads to spatial head specialization without annotations

title: InstantHMR : Real-Time Human Mesh Recovery on Your Phone
task: Real-time mobile human mesh recovery from single image
key_results: InstantHMR on Samsung Galaxy S23: 5.5 ms per person; on NVIDIA RTX 4070: 0.98 ms; 12× faster than only mobile competitor; 40.0 mm PA-MPJPE on 3DPW, competitive with state-of-the-art
comments: Excellent mobile deployment with comprehensive re-evaluation of 11 prior methods; latency gains are impressive, though accuracy trade-offs vs desktop models are non-trivial.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mobile inference on NPU/GPU enables real-time human mesh recovery
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 5.5 ms on mobile, 0.98 ms on GPU

title: Spatial Harness: Grounding Spatial Reasoning in Executable World States with Physics Engines
task: Grounding spatial reasoning in executable physics-engine world states
key_results: Spatial Harness on MindCube: improves Qwen3.5-27B from 52.70% to 71.14% (+7.52% over pySpatial); reaches 98.25% with perfect poses vs 71.81% model-internal reasoning
comments: Novel approach combining VLMs with physics-engine grounding; the dramatic improvement with perfect poses suggests perceptual bottleneck, not reasoning limitation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Explicit physics-engine grounding improves spatial reasoning accuracy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 71.14% vs 52.70% for Qwen3.5-27B

title: Stochastic Deep Supervision for Gallery-Consistent Early-Exit Face Recognition
task: Training Vision Transformers for budget-selected fixed-depth early exits in face recognition
key_results: SD-ViT: stays within 0.4 IJB-C points of full depth at full-depth accuracy; early-exit probes recover >96% performance at 50% cost; no gallery recomputation needed
comments: Elegant solution to early-exit FR; stochastic deep supervision is simple yet effective, though universal threshold across depths is practical but potentially suboptimal.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stochastic auxiliary supervision at intermediate blocks creates usable embeddings
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; early exits recover >96% of full-depth performance

title: All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States
task: Evaluating LLM ability to report injected internal pain states
key_results: Pain reports never exceed text-based revelation (excess <2.5% in 106/108 conditions); probes achieve 98-100% accuracy distinguishing pain from sadness; steering raises destructive actions without pain reports
comments: Sophisticated introspection experiment revealing mismatch between decodable and reportable states; important implications for value alignment and transparency, though limited to three models.

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLMs can report internal pain states they represent
hypotheses.result: Rejected; pain never reported above text-based revelation threshold

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pain steering is behaviorally consequential
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; raises destructive actions 3.5% → 48% in Qwen

title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application
task: Evaluating FlyHash for LLM agent external memory retrieval
key_results: FlyHash preserves neighbor structure better per bit than SimHash on 10 seeds, 4 datasets, 2 modalities; quality advantage does not translate to memory/latency savings; HNSW dominates both; FlyHash wins on agent-memory relevance labels
comments: Rigorous empirical validation with uncommon honesty about negative results; the practical case for hashing is narrower than quality metrics alone suggest.

hypotheses.hypothesis: FlyHash preserves neighbor structure better per bit than SimHash
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; robust across datasets and modalities

hypotheses.hypothesis: Quality advantage translates to memory/latency savings vs HNSW
hypotheses.result: Rejected; HNSW dominates at practical scale

hypotheses.hypothesis: FlyHash advantage survives agent-memory relevance labels
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; outperforms SimHash on non-circular labels

title: Horizon-Scalable Q-Learning
task: Learning long-horizon value functions by automatically balancing one-step and multi-step returns
key_results: Horizon-Scalable Q-Learning (HQL) avoids failures of both one-step and multi-step TD on combination-lock tasks; outperforms prior horizon-reduction methods on OGBench and OCBench long-horizon tasks
comments: Principled off-policy correction without action densities; though conceptually sound, empirical improvements over baselines on standard benchmarks remain modest.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Critic-guided multi-step extension enables accurate long-horizon value learning
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; HQL balances TD error accumulation on long-horizon tasks

title: PhysioWave-T: Token-Efficient Wavelet Foundation Models for Biosignals
task: Token-efficient wavelet foundation models for multi-modal biosignals (EEG, ECG, sEMG)
key_results: PhysioWave-T: 30M EEG encoder, 4.0–7.2× latency reduction, 6.8–12.7× peak memory savings via scale folding; leads 8/9 EEG metrics vs BENDR/BIOT/LaBraM/EEGPT; RALF multimodal fusion raises SeizeIT2 sensitivity from 61.4% to 74.4%
comments: Well-executed foundation model with strong efficiency gains; dynamic scale folding is elegant, though evaluation on seizure detection is encouraging but domain-specific.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dynamic scale folding reduces sequence length without accuracy loss
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 4–7.2× latency reduction while maintaining performance

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multimodal fusion improves seizure detection
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; RALF raises sensitivity from 61.4% to 74.4%

title: Prediction of the self-association of the nuclear inhibitor of DNA-binding and differentiation proteins
task: Predict ID protein self-association and heterodimerization mechanisms
key_results: ID1 forms stable homodimers and ID1-ID4 heterodimers via HLH domain interactions; dimer formation reduces nuclear concentration and functional activity
comments: The study relies entirely on computational predictions (MD and docking) without experimental validation of predicted binding interfaces or thermodynamic parameters.

inputs: ID1, ID2, ID3, ID4 protein structures
outputs: Conformational dynamics, stability metrics over 100 ns
Homodimer and heterodimer poses, binding interfaces

hypotheses.hypothesis: ID proteins self-associate through HLH domains to form stable dimers
hypotheses.result: ID1 homodimers and ID1-ID4 heterodimers predicted as stable via MD simulations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dimerization sequesters ID proteins from nucleus, reducing inhibitor function
hypotheses.result: Model predicts dimer formation lowers nuclear concentration of active monomers

title: TINAG suppresses renal cell carcinoma progression and angiogenesis by rebalancing mTORC1 signaling via integrin α3β1 receptor
task: Determine mechanism of TINAG suppression of renal cell carcinoma via integrin α3β1-mTORC1 axis
key_results: TINAG-integrin α3β1 binding suppresses mTORC1 activity in tumor and endothelial cells; TINAG inhibited RCC growth and metastasis including in sorafenib-resistant models; TINAG exhibited dual anti-angiogenic and anti-tumor effects
comments: Novel extracellular regulation of mTOR is intriguing, but the observation that integrin α3β1 with canonical ligands does not promote growth contrasts with classical integrin biology and merits deeper investigation into ligand-specific signaling.

model_io.model: RCC tumor cells; endothelial cells; in vivo RCC tumor models (wild-type and sorafenib-resistant)

hypotheses.hypothesis: TINAG binds integrin α3β1 to transduce negative signals that suppress mTORC1 activity
hypotheses.result: TINAG-integrin α3β1 interaction reduced mTORC1 signaling and cell proliferation/migration in RCC and endothelial cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: TINAG exerts dual inhibition on tumor and endothelial cells via integrin-mTORC1 axis
hypotheses.result: TINAG suppressed both RCC growth/metastasis and angiogenesis, including in sorafenib-resistant tumors

title: RSK2 and β-Trcp-mediated ubiquitination of FOXN3 impairs DNA damage and confers radioresistance in lung cancer
task: Characterize RSK2 and β-Trcp-mediated FOXN3 ubiquitination in lung cancer radioresistance
key_results: Reduced FOXN3 expression correlated with poor prognosis and radioresistance in lung adenocarcinoma; FOXN3 depletion impaired DNA damage response; RSK2 and β-Trcp collaboratively mediated FOXN3 ubiquitination via DSGYAS motif, attenuating DNA damage
comments: The mechanism elegantly links transcription factor degradation to radioresistance, but functional validation of the DSGYAS motif and RSK2-β-Trcp cooperation could benefit from additional biochemical and cellular assays.

model_io.model: Lung cancer cells (FOXN3-depleted vs control); lung adenocarcinoma patient samples

hypotheses.hypothesis: FOXN3 promotes BRCA1 transcription to enhance DNA damage response
hypotheses.result: FOXN3 binding to BRCA1 promoter increased BRCA1 transcription and DNA damage; FOXN3 depletion impaired DNA damage response

hypotheses.hypothesis: RSK2 and β-Trcp cooperatively ubiquitinate FOXN3 at DSGYAS motif to promote degradation and radioresistance
hypotheses.result: RSK2 and β-Trcp interacted with FOXN3 and facilitated its ubiquitination-mediated degradation, attenuating DNA damage and conferring radioresistance

title: ER–mitochondria contacts orchestrate mitochondrial transport via C19orf12
task: Determine role of C19orf12 in mitochondrial transport via ER-mitochondria contacts
key_results: C19orf12 loss causes perinuclear mitochondrial clustering and impaired anterograde neuronal transport; C19orf12-Miro1-Kif5b complex links ER-mitochondria contacts to microtubule-based transport
comments: Provides mechanistic insight into HSP pathogenesis through compartmentalized protein interactions, though Ca²⁺ modulation appears biphasic and may warrant further kinetic characterization.

model_io.model: C19orf12-knockout cells and neurons; C19orf12-deficient mice

hypotheses.hypothesis: C19orf12 scaffolds Miro1-Kif5b motor complex at ER-mitochondria contacts to enable anterograde transport
hypotheses.result: Loss of C19orf12 disrupts this complex and impairs transport; recombinant complex formation observed in vitro

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ca²⁺ modulates C19orf12-Miro1 interaction to regulate transport
hypotheses.result: Biphasic Ca²⁺-dependent association observed in vitro and biphasic mitochondrial motility in live cells

title: Shenling Baizhu San ameliorates MASLD complicated with sarcopenia-like muscle dysfunction in association with AMPKα signaling
task: Investigate Shenling Baizhu San amelioration of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease with sarcopenia via AMPKα
key_results: SLBZS treatment increased p-AMPKα/AMPKα and p-ACC/ACC ratios in liver and skeletal muscle; upregulated CPT-1 and downregulated SREBP-1C/FAS; decreased FOXO1/MAFbx expression; improved hepatic steatosis, grip strength, and muscle mass
comments: Clear mechanistic link to AMPKα activation as nutrient-sensor, but the HFHS rat model only partially recapitulates human MASLD-sarcopenia comorbidity and lacks metabolic complexity of systemic disease.

model_io.model: HFHS diet-induced MASLD with sarcopenia-like muscle dysfunction in rats

hypotheses.hypothesis: SLBZS enhances AMPKα signaling in liver and skeletal muscle to improve nutrient homeostasis and reduce lipid accumulation
hypotheses.result: SLBZS increased p-AMPKα/AMPKα and p-ACC/ACC ratios; upregulated CPT-1 and downregulated SREBP-1C/FAS in both tissues

hypotheses.hypothesis: Enhanced AMPKα signaling in skeletal muscle reduces protein degradation to preserve muscle mass
hypotheses.result: SLBZS decreased FOXO1 and MAFbx expression in skeletal muscle, correlating with improved grip strength and muscle mass

title: S-layer expansion is mediated by hoop-like cracks in the paracrystalline lattice during Bacillus anthracis growth
task: Elucidate S-layer lattice expansion mechanism via hoop-like cracks during Bacillus anthracis growth
key_results: S-layer expansion occurs via pervasive hoop-like cracks in the paracrystalline lattice; two modes of assembly (dispersed and focused) operate at cracks; local pulling forces from dispersed peptidoglycan synthesis cause crack formation
comments: High-resolution imaging elegantly reveals a previously hidden growth mechanism, though the mechanistic connection between pulling forces and crack nucleation remains phenomenological rather than quantitatively predictive.

model_io.model: Bacillus anthracis during logarithmic growth; in situ cryo-electron tomography

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dispersed peptidoglycan synthesis generates local pulling forces that create hoop-like cracks in the S-layer lattice
hypotheses.result: Pulse-chase experiments showed pervasive hoop-like cracks mediating S-layer expansion; dispersed and focused assembly modes observed at cracks

title: A conserved urate oxidase helix-tiling assembly promotes metabolic robustness in peroxisomes
task: Determine structural organization and functional role of urate oxidase assembly in peroxisomes
key_results: Urate oxidase assembles into helical fiber supramolecular architecture tiling laterally into porous lamellar scaffold; assembly abolished by structure-guided perturbation without altering intrinsic catalysis; assembled state enhances resistance to thermal, proteolytic, and oxidative stress
comments: Elegant demonstration that supramolecular organization confers robustness without trade-off to accessibility; conservation across mammals suggests evolutionary fitness benefit, though in vivo functional assays of substrate flux remain absent.

model_io.model: Mouse liver peroxisomes; in situ cryo-electron tomography; structure-guided perturbation mutants

hypotheses.hypothesis: Urate oxidase helix-tiling assembly enhances metabolic robustness in the peroxide-rich peroxisomal matrix
hypotheses.result: Assembled state showed increased resistance to thermal, proteolytic, and oxidative stress compared to non-assembled state while maintaining accessible surface area for substrate/product exchange

title: Dimethyl fumarate ameliorates imiquimod-induced psoriasiform inflammation and suppresses melanogenesis
task: Evaluate topical dimethyl fumarate efficacy in psoriasiform inflammation and melanogenesis
key_results: Topical DMF reduced PASI/BSA in patients with mild-to-moderate psoriasis; topical and intraperitoneal DMF comparably reduced inflammatory infiltration and epidermal hyperplasia; DMF suppressed tyrosinase and MITF expression, reducing melanin content
comments: Dual anti-inflammatory and anti-melanogenic effects are promising, but the 4-day mouse model is quite short-term and may not reflect chronic disease dynamics or long-term safety.

model_io.model: Imiquimod-induced psoriasiform mouse model (4 days); human keratinocytes; mouse melanocytes; ex vivo human skin

hypotheses.hypothesis: DMF suppresses NF-κB and STAT3 phosphorylation to reduce keratinocyte-derived inflammatory cytokines
hypotheses.result: DMF significantly reduced TNF-α, IL-17C mRNA and p-p65, p-STAT3 levels in keratinocytes stimulated with IL-36γ or M5

hypotheses.hypothesis: DMF inhibits melanogenesis by suppressing MITF and tyrosinase expression
hypotheses.result: DMF reduced tyrosinase activity and melanin content in melanocytes and attenuated UVB-induced melanogenesis in ex vivo skin

title: Cerium-quercetin nanoparticles: antioxidant properties and therapeutic performance in sepsis
task: Evaluate cerium-quercetin nanoparticles as antioxidant and anti-inflammatory therapy for sepsis
key_results: CQ NPs reduced intracellular ROS and apoptosis, increased Nrf2/HO-1 expression, decreased p-p65/p65 and p-IκBα/IκBα ratios; in CLP-induced sepsis mice, CQ NPs reduced TNF-α/IL-6/IL-1β and improved survival
comments: Dual antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects are therapeutic, but mechanism of macrophage CD86/CD206 rebalancing remains incompletely characterized and warrants deeper mechanistic analysis.

model_io.model: CQ NPs in vitro; CLP-induced sepsis mouse model

hypotheses.hypothesis: CQ NPs scavenge reactive oxygen/nitrogen species and suppress NF-κB signaling to reduce sepsis-associated inflammation
hypotheses.result: CQ NPs exhibited concentration-dependent ROS scavenging, reduced p-p65 and p-IκBα ratios, and decreased circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines in septic mice

title: Integrated intracellular and secretome proteomics reveal compartment-specific responses to plasma-treated water solutions combined with doxorubicin in hypopharyngeal carcinoma
task: Characterize intracellular and secretome proteomic responses to plasma-treated water plus doxorubicin in head and neck cancer
key_results: 80% of secreted proteins modified by PTWS+DOXO were not modified by DOXO alone; Air PTWS increased extracellular HSP70/HSP10/RAB11B while O₂ PTWS decreased 25 of 33 modified secreted proteins including cathepsin D and HSP27
comments: The study explicitly disclaims causal inference and emphasizes compartment-specific, formulation-dependent responses; secretome changes poorly reflected by intracellular proteomics, highlighting complementary information sources.

model_io.model: FaDu head-and-neck cancer cells; HaCaT keratinocytes

hypotheses.hypothesis: PTWS formulations (air vs O₂) elicit distinct secretome responses when combined with doxorubicin
hypotheses.result: Air PTWS+DOXO increased HSP70/HSP10/RAB11B; O₂ PTWS+DOXO predominantly reduced secreted protein abundance with 25/33 proteins decreased

title: Efficient count-based models improve power and robustness for large-scale single-cell eQTL mapping
task: Efficient pseudobulk single-cell eQTL mapping with count-based models
key_results: jaxQTL identifies 16% more eGenes than linear models; sc-eQTLs explain 9.90±0.88% SNP-heritability vs 6.10±0.76% bulk; fine-mapped sc-eQTLs enriched in cell-type-specific enhancers (P=3×10⁻¹⁰)
comments: Negative binomial modeling outperforms linear approaches for sparse counts; distal regulatory effects missed in bulk tissues; sc-eQTLs prioritize disease genes (IL6ST) improving GWAS-eQTL link.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Negative binomial model provides calibrated inference for sparse sc-RNA data

title: Explainable AI-based disease diagnostics using real-time plasmonic biosensor data and blockchain technology
task: Secure federated learning for biomedical diagnostics with blockchain and XAI
key_results: Improved diagnostic accuracy, enhanced security, scalable performance with acceptable latency overhead
comments: Privacy-preserving framework addresses real healthcare challenges but lacks quantitative performance metrics for comparison.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Blockchain prevents model poisoning attacks

title: Machine learning model using contrast-enhanced CT for predicting overall survival in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE plus targeted and immunotherapy: a multicenter study
task: ML prediction of overall survival in unresectable HCC with TACE+immunotherapy
key_results: Radscore from 6 features (Lasso Cox + RSF); radiomics-clinical model C-index 0.893 (training), 0.758 (internal validation), 0.74 (external); 1/2/3-year AUCs 0.731/0.7/0.756 externally
comments: Combined radiomics-clinical model improves OS prediction; HBV and vascular invasion independent predictors; external validation confirms practical utility for treatment response prediction.

model_io.model: Radiomics + clinical variables via Lasso Cox + Random Survival Forest
inputs: contrast-enhanced CT from 180 unresectable HCC patients (4 centers)

hypotheses.hypothesis: CECT radiomics improve OS prediction in TACE-ICIs-MTTs therapy

title: Preoperative prediction of lymphovascular invasion in breast cancer using multicenter DCE-MRI radiomics and clinical features
task: Multicenter radiomics for preoperative lymphovascular invasion prediction in breast cancer
key_results: Combined model AUC 0.856 (training), 0.721 (internal validation), 0.665 (external test 1), 0.603 (external test 2); LR/MLP most stable across centers; complex ensembles overfit
comments: Exceptional rigor with multicenter external validation revealing substantial performance degradation; calibration slopes decline externally (0.49-0.21), requiring local recalibration before deployment.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Radiomics improve LVI prediction over clinical variables alone
hypotheses.result: Supported internally; inconsistent external benefit; recalibration needed

hypotheses.hypothesis: Simple models (LR, MLP) generalize better than ensemble methods
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; complex methods overfit externally

title: Development and external validation of a machine learning model for 28-day mortality in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding and chronic kidney disease
task: ML prediction of 28-day mortality in GIB patients with CKD
key_results: LR model: AUC 0.734 (internal), 0.732 (external); 8 predictors selected (RDW, chloride, anion gap, PT, PTT, SBP, sepsis, COPD)
comments: Simple LR outperforms complex algorithms in external validation; sensitivity 45.5% and PPV modest indicate preliminary tool status requiring multicenter prospective validation.

inputs: 926 GIB+CKD patients from MIMIC-IV (training n=648, internal validation n=278) and 1000 from GDMUAH (external)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Clinical and laboratory variables predict mortality in GIB+CKD patients
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; LR AUC 0.732 externally with 8 features

hypotheses.hypothesis: Complex ensemble methods generalize better externally
hypotheses.result: Not supported; LR more robust than gradient boosting
